Bug_Title: SING: Class using singleton design pattern indirectly implements Cloneable interface. (SING_SINGLETON_INDIRECTLY_IMPLEMENTS_CLONEABLE)
Bug_Details:
If a class using singleton design pattern indirectly implements the Cloneable interface, it is possible to create a copy of the object, thus violating the singleton pattern.
Therefore, implementing the Cloneable interface should be avoided. If that's not possible because of an extended super-class, the solution would be overriding the clone method to unconditionally throw CloneNotSupportedException.

For more information, see: SEI CERT MSC07-J.
Bug_Explanation: The SingletonClass extends SuperClass which doesn't implement Cloneable interface directly. However, by implementing Cloneable in SingletonClass, it indirectly allows cloning, which violates the singleton pattern.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case attempts to clone the SingletonClass instance by calling the showBug() method, which is expected to throw a CloneNotSupportedException since the SingletonClass implements Cloneable indirectly. However, since the SingletonClass does not override the clone() method to throw this exception, the test case will not fail as expected, which will demonstrate the bug.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results confirm the presence of the bug. The test code successfully clones the singleton object, which is not supposed to be possible as per the singleton design pattern. This is a violation of the rule that a class using the singleton design pattern should not indirectly implement the Cloneable interface.
